findings.F1: In the falling calm profile (the book's own regime), when the close sat above its 20-day average, the deepest third of the stretches was followed by an unusual 5-day move of +4.19 % (t 2.42, 36 cases on 21 days) and an unusual 10-day move of +13.5 % (t 2.32, 28 cases on 16 days); the two shallower thirds showed only +0.80 % (t 0.54) and +0.04 % (t 0.02) over 5 days.
findings.F2: In falling markets, the same split with a calm proxy (30-day swing at or below the 60-day swing) shows closes above the average went on to an unusual 5-day move of +3.49 % (t 2.12, 63 cases, 28 days), and closes below it to −2.70 % (t −1.68, 185 cases, 65 days); falling bars in the highest stretch quintile gained +4.17 % (t 2.75, 34 cases, 17 days).
findings.F3: Across all bars, the unusual 5-day move rises in order with the stretch quintile: −1.73 % (t −1.01), −0.91 %, −0.47 %, +1.41 % (t 1.82), +2.20 % (t 1.79), with a Spearman correlation of 0.10 (1,622 cases). The stretch carries the price on; it does not pull it back.
findings.F4: The tested short is neither graded nor stable. Inside its profile, closes below the average gave unusual 5-day moves of 0.0 % (t 0.01), −3.79 % (t −2.84) and −2.89 % (t −1.38) from the shallowest third to the deepest. The short paid in 2018 and 2019 (−3.46 %, t −1.97; −3.23 %, t −2.40) and turned against the book in 2020 and 2021 (+1.87 %, +1.17 %).
findings.F5: The brief's own claim does not show in these folds. In falling agitated markets (proxy), closes below the average gave an unusual 5-day move of +0.61 % (t 0.25, 127 cases, 42 days). Across agitated bars (proxy), the lowest stretch quintile gave −1.79 % (t −0.53), not a rebound.
findings.F6: Weekday, year and 1-day-return groupings show nothing that stands out after this many looks. The largest is the second 1-day-return quintile at −2.38 % (t −2.26), with no order across the quintiles; weekdays range from −1.74 % to +2.09 % with every |t| at or below 1.21.

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the further a coin's close sits above its 20-day average, measured in units of the standard deviation of its daily returns over the same 20 days, the more it keeps rising over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy coins that push well above their average while the past two months have been falling and calm, and would buy more the larger the push, instead of fading it as a bounce in a downtrend.
ideas.name: falling calm stretch above rises
